messages:
Wei Chen: Heads up: doing a pass on the Quickstart Templates pages and I’m seeing a bunch of snippet drift vs `redwood-quickstarts`. Example: docs show `REDWOOD_API_KEY`, repo now uses `REDWOOD_API_KEY` + `REDWOOD_BASE_URL` (optional) + `REDWOOD_PROJECT` in the config loader. Also some code blocks lost indentation when rendered.

Elliot Price: ugh, yeah. Which pages? Is this the new quickstarts landing or the RAG walkthrough?

Wei Chen: both. Specifically `/quickstarts/rag/python` and `/quickstarts/agents/typescript`. In the Python page, we show:

```bash
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...
export MODEL=...
```

…but repo README has:

```bash
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...
export REDWOOD_MODEL=redwood/sonoma-chat
export REDWOOD_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS=30000
```

Also docs are still calling the client `Redwood()` but SDK changed to `RedwoodClient()` (I think from the helper work).

GitHub: PR opened by @wei-chen: redwood-docs#914 "Fix quickstart snippet drift + formatting" <https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-docs/pull/914>

Dana Lo: Confirm TS side: templates use `REDWOOD_MODEL` now, not `MODEL`. Also the snippet in docs still shows `fetch('/v1/chat/completions')` but template uses SDK helper + trace context propagation.

Monica Patel: On Python, SDK naming: it’s `from redwood import Redwood` (class name stayed), but the quickstarts wrapper we added is `get_client()` in `shared/redwood_client.py`. Docs should show the wrapper, not raw SDK, so we get retry/timeout defaults.

Ibrahim Khan: +1. Also the docs snippet currently omits streaming reconnection handling.

Wei Chen: yep. There’s also formatting issues: some fenced blocks are using ```ts but inside it has bash prompts, so the site formatter is doing weird quote/escape.

Elliot Price: can you link exact lines in docs where it’s wrong? I’ll help review the PR. Also, reminder: we said docs should be generated from repo snippets where possible, to avoid drift.

Wei Chen: in PR 914 I added inline comments, but quick pointers:
- `content/quickstarts/rag/python.mdx` lines ~42-75
- `content/quickstarts/agents/typescript.mdx` lines ~88-140
- `content/quickstarts/observability.mdx` traces section still shows `x-request-id` header but templates now set `x-redwood-request-id` (and echo back). Need to align.

Sabrina James: Wait, did we actually finalize header naming? I thought the templates send `x-request-id` and Redwood echoes `x-redwood-request-id` if missing?

Monica Patel: Current behavior per SDK helper: we accept `x-request-id` as input (if caller sets), otherwise generate and send `x-redwood-request-id`. Docs should recommend setting `x-request-id` at edge (nginx / gateway) and letting templates pass through.

Dana Lo: In TS template we’re doing:

```ts
const requestId = req.headers["x-request-id"] ?? crypto.randomUUID();
res.setHeader("x-request-id", requestId);
```

and then we pass it to Redwood as `x-request-id`. That gives us consistent correlation with the rest of app logs.

Wei Chen: ok, so doc should keep `x-request-id` for app-level, and mention Redwood will mirror into Console correlation fields. Right now the docs mention only `x-redwood-request-id` and it’s confusing.

Kira Thompson: +1 please. Also on the Dedicated/Private callouts: docs mention “Kubernetes optional” but the repo has manifests and we want to nudge people to those. Just don’t oversell it as production-ready.

Elliot Price: Re: snippet drift, can we switch the docs to use snippet extraction from the quickstarts repo? (like we do for SDK docs). Connor/Sahana — do we have the pipeline ready or still flaky?

Sahana Iyer: Snippet extraction exists but is a little brittle on path renames. It’s what broke the docs deploy last week (INT-811). If we keep it, we need:
1) stable snippet markers in repo
2) CI to fail PRs when markers move
3) pin to a tag (e.g., `redwood-quickstarts@v0.3.1`) instead of main

Connor O'Brien: Agree. For launch we pinned docs to the `v0.3.x` tag but a few pages were still hand-copied during the rush. We should move everything to extraction or accept periodic drift.

Wei Chen: For now PR 914 updates the docs inline and adds a note at top of each page: “These commands match redwood-quickstarts v0.3.2”. I can follow up with a separate PR to convert pages to snippet imports once the markers are stabilized.

Elliot Price: works. For formatting: please make sure code fences match language. We also need to avoid long lines in JSON examples; Prettier is wrapping badly.

Dana Lo: I can add snippet markers in the TS template README this afternoon if that helps extraction. Like:

```md
<!-- snippet:start:quickstart-env -->
...
<!-- snippet:end:quickstart-env -->
```

We’re already doing similar in another repo.

Sabrina James: Python side too. We can add markers around the `curl` examples + the `get_client()` usage.

Wei Chen: perfect. Another drift: docs show `REDWOOD_REGION` env var; template uses `REDWOOD_ROUTE` (routing policy) and region is implicit. Can we remove region mention from quickstarts and point to “Console routing / fallback” doc instead?

Monica Patel: yes please. Region tends to create support tickets (“I set region and now 404 / mismatch”). Route is the right abstraction.

Elliot Price: OK. Wei, in PR 914:
- update env var tables to match template contract (`REDWOOD_*`)
- align client creation to shared helper
- fix header guidance to `x-request-id`
- clean up code fence languages

Then we’ll do a follow-up task to move to snippet extraction once markers land.

Wei Chen: done. Also added a small “copy/paste test” checklist to PR description. If anyone can sanity check locally, that’d be great.

GitHub: @elliot-price approved redwood-docs#914

Sahana Iyer: I can run the docs preview build after merge. Please keep any snippet extraction changes separate so we can isolate failures.

Elliot Price: merging now. Thanks all.

GitHub: PR merged by @elliot-price: redwood-docs#914 "Fix quickstart snippet drift + formatting"
